title: Owen and the Moon's Wobbly Smile
markdown:
Owen loved facts. He loved the bright truth of the sun. But when night fell, shadows and whispers made his tummy jig with nerves. Dr. Hale asked him to build a platform to watch the moon. Owen shivered at the thought of the dark.

Suddenly, a moth, a speck of dust with wings, flitted near his shed light. "Shoo!" Owen yelped. It was Lyra, a shy flutter of silver, drawn to warmth. Her frantic dance made Owen’s stomach do a somersault. "The night is so wobbly!" he grumbled.

Dr. Hale found him. "Night giving you the jitters, Owen?" she asked, her voice a gentle hum.

"It's… unpredictable!" Owen blurted. "Like a puzzle missing half its pieces!"

Dr. Hale chuckled. "The night just plays by different rules," she said, pointing to the shy curve of the moon. "See that smile? Tonight it’s small, but soon it will be a great big cheese! The Moon plays a game of shadows with the Sun."

She led Owen to his unfinished platform. "Imagine this," she said, holding a grey stone. "You're here." She tapped Owen's toe. "The Sun is over there, a bright giant. The Moon? It's our stone friend, doing laps around us. We only see the part the Sun shines on. As it zooms around, we see different bits of its sunny face."

With dancing fingers, she showed him. A bright lamp (the Sun) and a small ball (Earth) and the stone (Moon) moved in a circle. Shadows stretched and vanished, making the stone look like it was shrinking and growing. "See?" Dr. Hale beamed. "Those are the moon phases! A grand, predictable dance, a celestial clockwork. It’s not changing shape; we just see its sunny smile change."

Owen stared. He looked from Dr. Hale’s model to the sliver in the sky. Then he looked at Lyra, still fluttering. She wasn’t a nighttime monster; she was just a tiny creature following light. Not spooky, just science. A thrill, not of fear but of understanding, zipped through him.

Over the next weeks, Owen watched. He tracked the moon’s slow journey, from a fingernail clipping to a magnificent, glowing orb. He watched Lyra visit his shed, a tiny dancer in the vast theatre of the night. He added a soft, warm lantern to his platform, a friendly beacon.

Finally, the platform stood sturdy and bright. Owen stood beside Dr. Hale, his heart beating with steady confidence. The moon, a perfect circle, hung like a pearl in the velvet sky. Lyra danced near the lantern, a silver whisper. A warmth spread through Owen. He had built something beautiful. He had learned the night held its own grand, predictable beauty. "It's amazing," he breathed. "It's all connected. The Earth, the Sun, the Moon... and even Lyra." He gazed upwards, his eyes wide with wonder. What other secrets were hidden in the sky, waiting for him to discover?
characters: Owen the patient builder, Lyra the moth, Dr. Hale
